title: Quarter plan cadence and cross-functional rhythm for private deliverables
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Establish a repeatable quarterly planning cadence that maps Private/VPC/On‑Prem roadmap items to company OKRs, defines cross‑functional sprint buckets, and documents gating criteria and risk mitigations for enterprise customer rollouts.
acceptance_criteria: Quarterly roadmap linked to OKRs with owners assigned
Cross‑functional sprint buckets published in calendar with milestones
Gate criteria for canary/enterprise waves documented
Risk register and mitigation plan approved by Security and Ops
updates: 2026-03-02: Kickoff with Eng/Design/Sales. Agreed on three sprint buckets (Core infra, Console UX, Compliance). Action: PMs to draft milestones and owner assignments.
2026-03-05: Draft milestone map posted to Confluence. Requested inputs from Dedicated capacity and Private infra teams by 2026-03-09.
2026-03-06: Security review — initial gating checklist includes KMS integration, audit logs, RBAC. Security requested a threat-model update; assigned to ENG-2987.
2026-03-09: Design review: console rollout flows need explicit rollback UI/ops hooks; created DES-682 for pattern spec. Link: https://design.example.com/console-rollout-patterns
2026-03-10: PM sync with Customer Success — identified three anchor customers for staged canaries. CS to prepare communication templates and SSO onboarding checklist.

2026-03-11: Eng flagged kernel backport risk affecting Core infra bucket; contingency plan: allow quantized model variant for early canary and run perf comparison dashboard. Added dependency ENG-4120.

2026-03-12: Prepared release window proposal and timeline. PR for milestone tracking: https://github.com/redwood-inference/private-deploy/pull/456. Next: finalize milestones and circulate to execs 2026-03-15.
risks: Kernel backport timelines could push infra deliverables beyond planned canary dates
Customer data migration windows may conflict with rollout waves causing rescheduling
Regulatory approvals in EMEA/APAC might delay availability in target regions
SRE staffing constraints during rollout weeks could affect incident response SLAs
